clue.text: Child catching more than half of city's fish

indicators.note: the child word holds the trimmed city word inside it, as if catching it

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: four-letter Latin word for city cut down to three letters, more than half of it

parts.note: URBS is Latin for city, familiar from Urbi et Orbi

explanation.surface: A youngster clutching most of a town's catch of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'city' wants an English city; it is the Latin word, as in the papal blessing Urbi et Orbi. 'more than half of' keeps three of its four letters and 'catching' puts them inside the child.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbot is a large flatfish prized for eating, an example of a fish.

clue.text: Burlesque effort involving a piece of underwear

indicators.note: the effort word wraps round the other pieces, involving them

parts.note: a try is an effort or attempt
a vest is an undershirt in British English

explanation.surface: A cabaret strip act built around one item of underclothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burlesque' suggests a striptease, but here it means a mocking parody. A British vest is an undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque imitation, as is a burlesque, a mocking parody of a serious work.

clue.text: Speciality of half of Spanish footballers

indicators.note: only the first half of the club's name is taken

parts.note: Real Madrid is a Spanish football club

explanation.surface: Half of a Spanish team's players have a particular strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes the first five of the ten letters of REAL MADRID.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a field or domain of expertise, a person's particular sphere.

clue.text: Old play I'm adapting in classical setting

indicators.note: adapting a work alters it, so the letters of play and I'm are rearranged

explanation.surface: A director reworking an old drama to stage it in an ancient Greek setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympia was the sanctuary of Zeus in ancient Greece where the Olympic Games were held.

clue.text: Organised workers' survey of Italian region

parts.note: organised workers form a trade union, abbreviated TU
to scan is to survey or look over

explanation.surface: A union carries out a survey of a part of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' looks like an anagram signal but belongs with 'workers' to make a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscany is a region of Italy; the adjective names things belonging to it, and a region is often called by it.

clue.text: Remorse after abandoning initial attempt to catch whopper

indicators.note: the remorse word comes after the trimmed hunt word
the first letter of the catching word is dropped

parts.note: to hunt is to try to catch prey
ruth is an old word for remorse or pity, as in ruthless

explanation.surface: An angler regrets a failed first attempt to land a huge fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whopper' looks like the big fish, but it is the definition, a big lie. 'abandoning initial' cuts HUNT to UNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A whopper is slang for a blatant lie, and a lie is a falsehood.

clue.text: Is left economist misrepresented?

indicators.note: the word economist is presented wrongly, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A query whether an economist on the political left has been misquoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as political, but 'Is left' means receives an inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into money is to inherit it, being left it in a will.

clue.text: Columnist channels online content

indicators.note: the letters are contained within channels online

explanation.surface: A newspaper columnist directs internet material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Columnist' suggests a journalist, but it is the admiral atop Nelson's Column in Trafalgar Square, London.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral Nelson stands on top of Nelson's Column, so he is jokingly one on a column.

clue.text: Agent taking one pound from sum received by actors

indicators.note: the trimmed sum word is taken in by the actors word, placed inside it

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a production

indicators.note: one pound is taken away from the sum word, removing that letter

parts.note: a tally is a running sum or count
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A theatrical agent docks a pound from the fee paid to performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' removes the pound sign's letter (Latin libra) from the sum word, and 'received by' places what is left inside the actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalyst is an agent that brings about change, especially a substance speeding a chemical reaction.

clue.text: Burns right for one giving sentimental performance

parts.note: torch and singe are two burns, both meaning to burn

explanation.surface: Robert Burns being the right choice for a mawkish turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burns' suggests the Scottish poet Robert Burns, but is the plural of two verbs, TORCH and SINGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch singer performs torch songs, sentimental ballads of unrequited love.

clue.text: Politician entering TV Centre for Songs of Praise?

indicators.note: the politician goes into the television word, entering it

parts.note: tele is a short word for television
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP walks into the BBC's Television Centre to take part in a hymn programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'TV Centre' looks like one place, the BBC's old London headquarters, but splits: TV is the container and 'Centre' starts the definition. Songs of Praise is a long-running BBC programme of hymns.
explanation.definitionFit: A temple is a place of worship, where hymns of praise are sung; the question mark flags a definition by example.

clue.text: Country without any trace of culture?

indicators.note: the country loses the letters of the word any, going without them

parts.note: Germany is a European country

explanation.surface: A nation said to have no culture at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without any trace of culture' reads as a sneer at a country, but 'any' is removed from GERMANY.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ is a microbe, the sort of tiny organism grown in a laboratory culture.

clue.text: Musicians making an impact by swearing interminably about nothing

parts.note: per means by, as in per post

indicators.note: the trimmed swearing word goes round the zero, sitting about it
without its end, so the last letter of the swearing word is dropped

parts.note: cussing is swearing
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Players who get noticed by cursing endlessly about nothing in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminably' cuts CUSSING to CUSSIN, and 'about' puts it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: The percussion section are the orchestra's drummers and players of other instruments that are struck.

clue.text: Seedy haunt in which, after time, I turn marauder

indicators.note: the other pieces are placed in the jumbled haunt letters
seedy means shabby or disreputable, so the letters of haunt are knocked about
the I and turn pieces follow the time letter

parts.note: a lathe is a machine for turning wood or metal

explanation.surface: In a sleazy dive, a man gets fed up with waiting and becomes a raider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seedy' jumbles haunt and splits it in two, 'in which' fills the gap, and 'after' puts I and the turning machine after the time letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth-century leader of the Huns ravaged the Roman Empire, a byword for a plundering raider.

clue.text: Come together in Spain after goal upset

indicators.note: the Spain letter comes after the jumbled goal word
the goal word is upset, its letters overturned into a new order

parts.note: a target is a goal or aim
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A football match in Spain, where the team rallies after a disputed goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges TARGET (goal) into TEGRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate is to combine into a whole, uniting the parts.

clue.text: Beneficiary of drone flying over Vatican?

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the first piece above the second
flying here means the letters of drone are sent in another direction

parts.note: the Holy See is the Pope's jurisdiction, based at the Vatican

explanation.surface: A beneficiary of a drone flying over the Vatican city.
explanation.definitionFit: An endorsee is the person to whom a cheque or bill is signed over, so its beneficiary.

clue.text: There's no going back after this — it's where you put your hand in your pocket!

definitions.text: There's no going back after this
definitions.meaning: the critical moment after which a change cannot be reversed

definitions.text: it's where you put your hand in your pocket!
definitions.meaning: read literally, the point at which you give a tip, reaching for money

explanation.surface: A moment of commitment, from which there is no retreat, likened to reaching for your wallet.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: the moment you hand over a gratuity.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the threshold beyond which a process becomes irreversible, and punningly a moment for leaving a gratuity.

clue.text: Short news item perhaps — Elvis occupying space?

parts.note: par is short for paragraph, a short item in a newspaper
Elvis Presley was known as the King of rock and roll

explanation.surface: A brief newspaper item asks if Elvis is in outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'space' suggests the cosmos, but it is a parking space.
explanation.definitionFit: Parking is putting a vehicle in a bay; the question mark shows it as filling a space.

clue.text: One supervising submerged navy swimmer

indicators.note: the navy letters are submerged, put down inside the guard word

parts.note: a guard is someone who watches over and supervises
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A lifeguard watching over a sunken navy diver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' suggests a person, but it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The gurnard is a sea fish with a large bony head, swimming along the bottom.

clue.text: Get old faster, perhaps, with loss of power

definitions.meaning: to age faster than someone is to ... them, a playful verb
a power cut, when electricity fails

explanation.surface: Ageing quicker with a loss of strength.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading invents a verb, like outrun: to outdo someone at ageing.
explanation.definitionFit: An outage is a period when electricity supply is cut, and the playful verb means to age more than another.

clue.text: Bird, one moving round capital

indicators.note: the mover word wraps round the capital, which sits inside it

parts.note: a budger is one who budges, one moving
Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: A bird fluttering about a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one moving' is a made-up agent noun, one who budges; 'round' wraps it around the Latvian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The budgie is a small Australian parakeet, a bird often kept as a pet.

clue.text: Ring Christopher's friend back

indicators.note: the friend's name is read backwards, back to front

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is the bear friend of Christopher Robin in A. A. Milne's stories

explanation.surface: A request to phone a friend named Christopher in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' reads as a phone call, but it is the definition, a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoop is a circular band, a ring of metal or wood.

clue.text: Cloth with which to cover onion bhaji when cooked

definitions.text: Cloth with which to cover onion
definitions.note: onion is slang for the head, so this is a head covering

indicators.note: cooking changes the ingredients, so the letters of bhaji are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cloth placed over an onion bhaji once it has been cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'onion bhaji' looks like one Indian snack; 'onion' is slang for head and ends the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hijab is a headscarf worn by some Muslim women, a cloth that covers the head.

clue.text: Setter's regrettably rejected sausage

indicators.note: the pieces are turned back, rejected and read in reverse

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I, so setter's is I'm
alas is an exclamation of regret

explanation.surface: The setter sadly sends back a sausage he did not like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns IM ALAS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, highly seasoned Italian sausage served in slices.

clue.text: To calibrate study's fair

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it; the 's stands for is
just means fair

explanation.surface: A judgment that a study is fair to calibrate an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Recalibrating an instrument means adjusting it again, setting it right once more.

clue.text: Come out of European Union right away?

indicators.note: the letter for right is taken away from the union word

parts.note: a merger is a union of two companies

explanation.surface: A question about leaving the European Union straight away, Brexit-style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European Union' looks like one body, but splits into E and MERGER, from which 'away' removes R.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out into view, appearing from somewhere hidden.

clue.text: To eat in bed, lie awkwardly

indicators.note: lying awkwardly means the letters of bed and lie are put in a clumsy new order

explanation.surface: Lying awkwardly in bed to have a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fit to eat is edible, safe and suitable as food.
